exposure: National surveillance activity (current, mandatory, voluntary, not offered)
outcome: Estimated SSI burden (total SSIs per annum)
cohort: The study analysed SSI surveillance data from National Health Service (NHS) hospitals in England covering 23 surgical procedures and included a survey of 84 English NHS hospitals.
finding: Current national surveillance activities and hospital-reported priorities were not associated with SSI rate, volume, or cost, with the highest contributors of SSIs and related costs (large bowel surgery and caesarean section) having limited or no national surveillance coverage.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was identified as the second highest contributor of total SSIs per annum (17,000 or 16%), but had no national surveillance coverage.
